For a stir-fry where you need to replace soy sauce due to a soy allergy, the best alternative that maintains the savory, umami flavor profile is coconut aminos. It is made from the sap of coconut blossoms and salt, offering a similar salty-sweet taste without the soy or gluten. Another option is tamari if the allergy is strictly to soy proteins but not gluten, though many with soy allergies also avoid it, so coconut aminos is the safer bet. You can also use a mixture of beef or mushroom broth with a splash of vinegar and a pinch of salt to mimic the depth of flavor.
